input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind for the Servicer/Marketing Agent/Custodian. The only occurrences of \"insurance\" are Obligor premium charges billed to wireless accounts (p0095) and FDIC deposit insurance in the account-eligibility definition (p0903); neither imposes any coverage obligation on Cellco. Cellco services the Receivables and holds Obligor account, payment and Receivable File data, so the absence of any E&O or cyber cover falls in walk-away territory under this rule. We therefore insert a short covenant at the end of Article X (Miscellaneous) at the fallback level only — errors and omissions of $1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of $2,000,000 — rather than the preferred CGL/E&O/cyber/workers' compensation programme, which is the smallest complete change.

ops.text: Section 10.14 Insurance. The Servicer will maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $1,000,000 and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We add a short insurance covenant in Article X because the Agreement has none, even though the Servicer handles Obligor account and payment data. This sits at our fallback position (E&O of $1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of $2,000,000); we can discuss our preferred limits if you prefer a fuller programme.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 10.14 requiring Servicer E&O insurance of $1,000,000 and cyber/privacy insurance of $2,000,000.

mappings.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
